section: Vedic literature - four Vedas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads, Vedangas, Sutras
subsections: Earliest literary references to the Andhras
Grammar and Vedanga works → author; six Vedangas

accepted.s: The earliest literary reference to the Andhras occurs in which of the following texts?
accepted.x: The word ‘Andhra’ first occurs in the Aitareya Brahmana, in the story of Sunahshepa.
accepted.tq: Identify the earliest occurrence by distinguishing the primary source from later references.
accepted.sec: Earliest literary references to the Andhras

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the literary references to the Andhras:
1. The Mahabharata states that the Andhras sided with the Kauravas.
2. The Arthashastra mentions the Andhras as a political entity.
3. The Rajatarangini refers to the Andhra region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Mahabharata, Arthashastra and Rajatarangini provide these respective references to the Andhras.
accepted.tq: Check each source separately before selecting the combined statement option.
accepted.sec: Earliest literary references to the Andhras

accepted.s: In the Sunahshepa story of the Aitareya Brahmana, Vishvamitra cursed his sons who refused to accept Sunahshepa to become what?
accepted.x: Vishvamitra cursed the fifty sons who refused to accept Sunahshepa to become non-Aryan peoples, including the Andhras, Pundras and Pulindas.
accepted.tq: Link the event, person and consequence in the narrative source.
accepted.sec: Earliest literary references to the Andhras

accepted.s: Which one of the following texts does NOT mention the Andhras?
accepted.x: The Rigveda does not mention the Andhras. The Mahabharata, Arthashastra and Rajatarangini contain references to them.
accepted.tq: Find the textual exception by separating the earliest reference from the absent reference.
accepted.sec: Earliest literary references to the Andhras

accepted.s: Megasthenes’ Indica credits the Andhras with which of the following combinations?
o: 50 fortified towns and a standing navy
30 fortified towns and a large army
40 fortified towns and a small navy
20 fortified towns and a large cavalry
accepted.x: Megasthenes’ Indica describes the Andhras as possessing 30 fortified towns and a large army.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired numerical description rather than one figure in isolation.
accepted.sec: Earliest literary references to the Andhras

accepted.s: The Andhras are named among the peoples within the Mauryan Empire in which inscription of Ashoka?
accepted.x: Ashoka’s Rock Edict XIII names the Andhras among the peoples within his empire.
accepted.tq: Match the people with the specific inscription rather than the ruler alone.
accepted.sec: Earliest literary references to the Andhras

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Katyayana composed the Varttika, critical notes on Panini’s grammar. Mahabhashya is associated with Patanjali, Nirukta with Yaska and Ashtadhyayi with Panini.
accepted.tq: Use author–work discrimination and eliminate swapped authors.
accepted.sec: Grammar and Vedanga works → author; six Vedangas

accepted.s: Nirukta, associated with Yaska, primarily deals with which subject?
accepted.x: Nirukta is the earliest extant work on etymology and is associated with Yaska.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the subject of a Vedanga work from the subjects of the other limbs.
accepted.sec: Grammar and Vedanga works → author; six Vedangas

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Vedanga)
 a. Shiksha
 b. Kalpa
 c. Chandas
 d. Jyotisha

List-II (Subject)
 i. Astronomy
 ii. Phonetics
 iii. Metrics
 iv. Rituals

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Shiksha is phonetics, Kalpa is rituals, Chandas is metrics and Jyotisha is astronomy.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a subject swap.
accepted.sec: Grammar and Vedanga works → author; six Vedangas

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct set of the six Vedangas?
o: Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chandas and Jyotisha
Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda, Kalpa and Nirukta
Ayurveda, Dhanurveda, Gandharvaveda, Shilpaveda, Kalpa and Yoga
Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Yoga, Sankhya, Mimamsa and Vedanta
accepted.x: The six Vedangas are Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chandas and Jyotisha.
accepted.tq: Separate the six Vedangas from the four Upavedas and six philosophical systems.
accepted.sec: Grammar and Vedanga works → author; six Vedangas

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Shilpa Veda deals with architecture, not astronomy. The other three pairs correctly describe the Upavedas.
accepted.tq: Find the single subject substitution within a familiar classification.
accepted.sec: Grammar and Vedanga works → author; six Vedangas

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Darsana)
 a. Nyaya
 b. Vaisheshika
 c. Sankhya
 d. Purva Mimamsa

List-II (Founder or principal teacher)
 i. Jaimini
 ii. Gautama
 iii. Kapila
 iv. Kanada

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Nyaya is associated with Gautama, Vaisheshika with Kanada, Sankhya with Kapila and Purva Mimamsa with Jaimini.
accepted.tq: Match philosophical systems through their associated teachers, checking each pair independently.
accepted.sec: Grammar and Vedanga works → author; six Vedangas

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Patanjali is associated with Yoga. Uttara Mimamsa is associated with Badarayana, Nyaya with Gautama and Vaisheshika with Kanada.
accepted.tq: Detect the swapped authorities in closely related philosophical schools.
accepted.sec: Grammar and Vedanga works → author; six Vedangas

accepted.s: The Shrauta Sutras primarily deal with which of the following?
accepted.x: Shrauta Sutras deal with public rituals and large sacrifices.
accepted.tq: Distinguish public ritual texts from domestic, legal and geometrical Sutras.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sutras:
1. Grihya Sutras deal with domestic rites and practices.
2. Dharma Sutras deal with laws and social practice.
3. Sulba Sutras deal with the measurement and construction of altars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Grihya, Dharma and Sulba Sutras respectively concern domestic rites, law and social practice, and altar construction.
accepted.tq: Map each Sutra to its distinctive practical subject before choosing the code.

accepted.s: Which of the following authors is associated with the Sulba Sutras?
accepted.x: Baudhayana is one of the authors associated with the Sulba Sutras; Apastamba, Katyayana and Manava are also associated with them.
accepted.tq: Identify the author from the specific Sutra tradition rather than from grammar or philosophy.

accepted.s: The theorem now known as the Pythagoras theorem is stated in the Sulbasutra of which author?
accepted.x: Baudhayana’s Sulbasutra contains the rule corresponding to the theorem now known as the Pythagoras theorem.
accepted.tq: Link the mathematical contribution with the specific author, not merely the general school.

accepted.s: The primary purpose of the Sulba Sutras was to provide rules for:
o: Interpreting the meaning of philosophical doctrines
accepted.x: Sulba Sutras contain rules for the measurement and construction of sacrificial altars.
accepted.tq: Apply the technical function of a text to a practical construction situation.

accepted.s: Which Veda is associated with the Hotri priest?
accepted.x: The Hotri was the reciter associated with the Rigveda.
accepted.tq: Match each Veda with the priest who performed its characteristic role.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Veda)
 a. Rigveda
 b. Samaveda
 c. Yajurveda
 d. Atharvaveda

List-II (Priest)
 i. Brahman
 ii. Adhvaryu
 iii. Hotri
 iv. Udgatri

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: The Rigveda was recited by the Hotri, Samaveda chanted by the Udgatri, Yajurveda executed by the Adhvaryu and Atharvaveda supervised by the Brahman priest.
accepted.tq: Begin with the familiar Rigveda–Hotri pair and complete the remaining functional matches.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Gopatha is the Brahmana associated with the Atharvaveda. Jaiminiya is associated with the Samaveda.
accepted.tq: Use the Veda–Brahmana association to detect the swapped text.

accepted.s: The Shatapatha Brahmana belongs to which branch of the Yajurveda?
accepted.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana belongs to the Shukla Yajurveda, while the Taittiriya Brahmana belongs to the Krishna Yajurveda.
accepted.tq: Separate the two Yajurveda branches by associating Shatapatha with Shukla.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Atharvaveda?
accepted.x: Gopatha is the Brahmana of the Atharvaveda, and Mundaka is one of its associated Upanishads.
accepted.tq: Pair the Veda with both its Brahmana and Upanishadic tradition.

accepted.s: Which of the following Upanishads is associated with the Samaveda?
accepted.x: Kena and Chandogya are associated with the Samaveda. Isha and Katha are associated with the Yajurveda, while Mundaka is associated with the Atharvaveda.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Upanishadic affiliations across the four Vedic traditions.

accepted.s: Which of the following groups consists only of Upanishads associated with the Yajurveda?
accepted.x: Brihadaranyaka, Isha, Katha, Taittiriya and Shvetashvatara are associated with the Yajurveda.
accepted.tq: Test the entire group for a single misplaced Upanishad rather than checking one name alone.

accepted.s: Brahmanas are best described as:
o: Philosophical dialogues concerned exclusively with the jnana-marga
Prose ritual commentaries concerned with the karma-marga
accepted.x: Brahmanas are prose ritual commentaries or liturgies and are associated with the karma-marga.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ritual function of Brahmanas from the philosophical role of Upanishads.

accepted.s: Which statement best describes the Aranyakas?
o: They are forest texts forming a bridge from karmamarga to jnanamarga.
They are domestic law books for householders.
They are astronomical tables independent of Vedic literature.
They are collections of military instructions.
accepted.x: Aranyakas are ‘forest texts’, generally concluding parts of the Brahmanas and forming a bridge from ritualism to philosophical speculation.
accepted.tq: Apply the transition function of Aranyakas between ritual and knowledge traditions.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vedic textual layers:
1. Brahmanas are primarily prose ritual commentaries.
2. Aranyakas are known as forest texts.
3. Brahmanas, Aranyakas and Upanishads form part of Shruti along with the Samhitas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The four layers of Vedic literature—Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas and Upanishads—are regarded as Shruti.
accepted.tq: Combine definitions with the structural classification of Vedic literature.

accepted.s: Which one of the following features is associated with the Shatapatha Brahmana?
o: It is the sole Brahmana of the Atharvaveda.
It is a grammar text attributed to Panini.
It narrates the eastward movement from Kuru-Panchala to Videha.
It deals exclusively with domestic rites.
accepted.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana narrates the spread of culture eastward from Kuru-Panchala to Videha.
accepted.tq: Associate a distinctive narrative feature with the correct Brahmana.

accepted.s: Which of the following subjects or events is mentioned in the Shatapatha Brahmana?
o: The conquest of Kalinga by Ashoka
The origin of the Sangam assemblies
accepted.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana mentions the Great Flood, besides describing the eastward spread of culture.
accepted.tq: Identify the unique narrative association instead of choosing a later historical event.

accepted.s: According to the descriptions associated with the Shatapatha Brahmana, which of the following is also mentioned?
o: The eastern and western seas and the first reference to money-lending
The use of iron coins by the Satavahanas
The foundation of the Mauryan Empire
accepted.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana mentions the eastern and western seas and contains the first reference to money-lending in the stated tradition.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive cluster of details attached to one text to reject later historical distractors.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Jaiminiya Aranyaka is associated with the Samaveda. Aitareya belongs to the Rigveda, while Brihadaranyaka and Taittiriya belong to the Yajurveda tradition.
accepted.tq: Match the less frequently tested Aranyaka names with their Vedic affiliations.
